        <section class="content article-content mb-6" itemprop="articleBody">
          <p>The Google Ads connector tools in Optimizely Opal give you direct access to your advertising performance data. Use them to retrieve detailed metrics across campaigns, ad groups, and individual keywords. This integration lets you analyze audience demographics, geographic trends, and search queries to understand how your audience interacts with your ads. By centralizing these insights, you can optimize your budgets and refine targeting for Performance Max and Shopping campaigns. This supports data-backed experimentation and drives higher return on investment (ROI).</p><p>First, an <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/36359944449805" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Opal administrator</a> must <a href="#h_01K8VBDBEWF17NE7XV6EC8CG70">connect Opal with Google Ads</a>. After an administrator installs the connector in Optimizely Connect Platform (OCP), you can <a href="#h_01KKCNWPHE41X467Y5YG4C9WV7">log in to Google Ads</a> from Opal to access your data. Administrators only need to install the Google Ads connection in OCP once.</p><h2 id="h_01KKCTFGB8MSSJTHHTBYD0JBJX">Use cases<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KKCTFGB8MSSJTHHTBYD0JBJX"></a></h2><p>The following use cases show how you can use Google Ads connector tools in Opal to connect ad performance data with content and creative workflows.</p><h3 id="h_01KKCV15C39HR1NTJWDYZ8KTS4">Marketing strategy and performance optimization<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KKCV15C39HR1NTJWDYZ8KTS4"></a></h3><p><strong>Goal</strong> – Data-driven budget allocation and campaign scaling.</p><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e28754d768b85a2fe17eeb7748a765fcd">
<strong>Key performance indicator (KPI) monitoring and budget shifting</strong> – Use the <code>googleads_get_campaigns</code> and <code>googleads_get_budgets</code> tools to identify campaigns with high conversion rates but low impression share (the percentage of eligible impressions your ads receive). Opal can draft a recommendation to reallocate funds from budget-constrained campaigns.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eaa5cedfadcc79752a30725ffa91345fa">
<strong>High-intent keyword discovery</strong> – Run the <code>googleads_get_keywords</code> and <code>googleads_get_search_terms</code> tools to surface high-value search queries that drive conversions but are not yet added as exact-match keywords.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e94b10d8f58eb60f0e8c5d5c71c0caff8">
<strong>Channel synergy analysis</strong> – Compare performance across Search, Shopping (<code>googleads_get_shopping_performance</code>), and Performance Max (PMax) (<code>googleads_get_asset_groups</code>) to determine which network is most efficient for specific product categories.</li>
</ul><h3 id="h_01KQHZMVCPSAZEP4MQMPKCHQPD">A/B experimentation<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KQHZMVCPSAZEP4MQMPKCHQPD"></a></h3><p><strong>Goal</strong> – Validate creative and copy hypotheses.</p><ul data-tight="true">
<li data-list-item-id="e3d5372c60fc4c67faab7186c1faae57c">
<strong>Ad copy comparison</strong> – Use the <code>googleads_get_ads</code> tool to compare the click-through rate (CTR) and conversion rate of different Responsive Search Ads (RSAs). Opal can analyze which headlines or descriptions drive performance and suggest variations for follow-up testing.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edebe03d1415c303fb70d47e10e957bd3">
<strong>Landing page validation</strong> – Correlate specific ad groups (<code>googleads_get_adgroups</code>) with conversion data to see which landing pages (mapped to those ad groups) are underperforming. Use this to trigger an Optimizely Web Experimentation or Optimizely Feature Experimentation test on those pages.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e4d7a6c3cd0e0daffa1ee4837b4751e16">
<strong>Demographic sensitivity testing </strong>– Use the <code>googleads_get_age_performance</code> and <code>googleads_get_gender_performance</code> tools to see if a specific creative resonates better with certain age groups. If a "Gen Z" creative is underperforming with its target, Opal can draft a brief for a more aligned creative direction.</li>
</ul><h3 id="h_01KQHZMVCQMDTHWB3WDRCBDE97">Content pipeline and creative plans<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KQHZMVCQMDTHWB3WDRCBDE97"></a></h3><p><strong>Goal</strong> – Use search data to fuel Optimizely Content Marketing Platform (CMP).</p><ul data-tight="true">
<li data-list-item-id="e9e02e8dca82a01c716725f8fa345f881">
<strong>Search-driven content briefs</strong> – Analyze top-performing search terms using the <code>googleads_get_search_terms</code> tool. If a specific question or pain point appears frequently, Opal can generate a brief for a blog post in CMP to address that topic through organic search content.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e87167d65d16bf434662f0825d5fd5fd0">
<strong>PMax asset optimization</strong> – Use the <code>googleads_get_asset_groups</code> tool to identify which asset groups in a Performance Max campaign have "Low" performance ratings. Opal can then help generate image prompts or headlines to replace the weak assets.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e4cb849e9a295cf3bb6fd50a5efaefb63">
<strong>Seasonal creative refresh</strong> – Pull geographic performance data using the <code>googleads_get_geographic_performance</code> tool. If a region is showing an uptick in interest for a specific product, use Opal to create localized ad copy or social assets tailored to that region's trends.</li>
</ul><h3 id="h_01KQHZMVCQ0B6XA3A2BZDMHK42">Audience insights and target strategy<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KQHZMVCQ0B6XA3A2BZDMHK42"></a></h3><p><strong>Goal</strong> – Refine your audience and your geography.</p><ul data-tight="true">
<li data-list-item-id="e5e209a8bc4f1251d666252aeafc44803">
<strong>Geographic expansion </strong>– Identify cities or regions with high conversion rates but low volume using the <code>googleads_get_geographic_performance</code> tool. Use this insight to create localized landing page content or localized ad extensions.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed01bf29619521a491364063173a4241d">
<strong>Audience mapping</strong> – Use the <code>googleads_get_audiences</code> tool to see which user lists are assigned. Opal can suggest <strong>Similar Segments</strong> or <strong>In-Market</strong> audiences based on the characteristics of the customers who convert at the highest rate.</li>
</ul><h2 id="h_01K8VBDBEWF17NE7XV6EC8CG70">Connect Opal with Google Ads<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01K8VBDBEWF17NE7XV6EC8CG70"></a></h2><h3 id="h_01KKC744XBD3CEE52R72N99D5K">Install the Opal Google Ads Tool in OCP<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KKC744XBD3CEE52R72N99D5K"></a></h3><p>In the OCP <strong>App Directory</strong>, complete the following:</p><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="e52d98e43570b7f89897bb06043f35157">
<p>Click the <strong>Opal Google Ads Tool</strong>.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1714/1160;" src="/hc/article_attachments/45868019597325" alt="Screenshot of the OCP App Directory with the Opal Google Ads Tool tile highlighted." width="1714" height="1160" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8d334be60949218dede9130589e65a0c">
<p>Click <strong>Install App</strong>.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 962/604;" src="/hc/article_attachments/45868019598093" alt="Screenshot of the Opal Google Ads Tool Overview with the Install App button highlighted." width="962" height="604" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
</ol><h3 id="h_01KKC7B334QC0GGNHJW16XQ0J2">Configure Google Ads API authentication<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KKC7B334QC0GGNHJW16XQ0J2"></a></h3><p>Configure the Google Ads API authentication so Opal can call Google Ads on behalf of your account.</p><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="e0cdfe22f7b613fc95567e5ac8b3ba63d">Select the <strong>Settings</strong> tab.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ece0ab3653e3fdf9cd4ea90cb47d40c2a">Expand the <strong>Google Ads API Authentication</strong> section.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efbcdb716eff60f83a0c6bf5f41a3da9e">Enter your <strong>Customer ID</strong>. See <a href="https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1704344?hl=en" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Find your Google Ads customer ID</a> in the Google documentation for instructions.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efa3cac7de3c1a24bb0dd7a4940697857">(Optional) Enter your <strong>Login Customer ID</strong>. If you manage multiple Google Ads accounts under a Manager account (a single login that controls several customer accounts), this is the Manager account ID. To find it, see the Additional tips to find your customer ID section in the <a href="https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1704344?hl=en" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Find your Google Ads customer ID</a> in the Google documentation.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7718289eb76b1d6e30bad7b6f16f65ba">
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1306/834;" src="/hc/article_attachments/45868019601293" alt="Screenshot of the Google Ads configuration in OCP with the Google ads API Authentication section expanded with the Save button highlighted." width="1306" height="834" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
</ol><h3 id="h_01KEJDK4GBA19AQV4ENMWND9AK">Configure tool permissions<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KEJDK4GBA19AQV4ENMWND9AK"></a></h3><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="e9db57c6d63270b6ceb3cfa2e46910e35">Select the <strong>Settings</strong> tab.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1bd257822cbeb1d9f09359214627c8da">Expand the <strong>Tool Permissions</strong> section.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e70d82b15d54162eef6e8eee7bc6bcc9c">Toggle <strong>Enable Data Reading</strong> on to enable read-only tools.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec08976032b04ca652279b8db3e5e3f3a">Toggle <strong>Enable Data Modifications</strong> on to enable write tools.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee19e17ae7e155d0f5be4a0dc49603517">
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1302/576;" src="/hc/article_attachments/45868194896269" alt="Google Ads OCP configuration with the Tools Permissions section expanded." width="1302" height="576" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
</ol><h3 id="h_01KRM3AVD8W0S2WS912GJFH3ED">Add the Google Ads connector tools to Opal<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KRM3AVD8W0S2WS912GJFH3ED"></a></h3><p>After you <a href="#h_01K8VBDBEWF17NE7XV6EC8CG70">install the app in OCP</a>, <a href="#h_01KKC7B334QC0GGNHJW16XQ0J2">configure Google Ads API authentication</a>, and <a href="#h_01KEJDK4GBA19AQV4ENMWND9AK">configure tool permissions</a>, complete the following in OCP to connect to Opal:</p><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="e1f563e6f25ff7dee7832852e50d521ca">Select the <strong>Settings </strong>tab.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8fada021b3faeb913c92e56a4706aef2">Expand <strong>Add to Opal</strong>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e392664022942bbc76bcc0a4a83b3d3a6">
<p>Click <strong>Add to Opal</strong> for the <strong>Opal Account</strong> you want to add the Google Ads connector tools to.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1372/564;" src="/hc/article_attachments/44179159625741" alt="Screenshot of the OCP Add to Opal settings page where Add to Opal is selected for an Opal account." width="1372" height="564" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
</ol><p>Click <strong>Remove from Opal </strong>to remove the connection.</p><p>After you complete the steps in this section, each Opal user in your account can follow the steps in <a href="#h_01KKCNWPHE41X467Y5YG4C9WV7">Authenticate with Google Ads</a> to connect their own Google Ads login.</p><h2 id="h_01KKCNWPHE41X467Y5YG4C9WV7">Authenticate with Google Ads<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KKCNWPHE41X467Y5YG4C9WV7"></a></h2><p>After an administrator <a href="#h_01K8VBDBEWF17NE7XV6EC8CG70">connects Opal with Google Ads</a>, log in from Opal to access your data. The Google Ads connector tools use user-level authentication, so you can only access data you have permission to view in Google Ads.</p><p>To authenticate, complete the following steps in Opal:</p><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="e8500e23a9578465b962f4c5ed9e9100b">Go to <strong>Tools > Connectors</strong>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edcd5f42dd9c7bcb18a80f1b38a55004c">
<p>Click <strong>Connect</strong> on the <strong>Google Ads</strong> connector tools.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 2348/856;" src="/hc/article_attachments/44179139937805" alt="Screenshot of the Opal Connectors page where Connect is selected on the Google Ads connector." width="2348" height="856" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb7b0143abbba97271038eb17d5eb8129">
<p>Log in to Google in the window Optimizely displays.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image wysiwyg-image-resized" style="width: 75%;"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1734/954;" src="/hc/article_attachments/44247663968013" alt="Screenshot of the Google sign-in window Optimizely displays during Google Ads authentication." width="1734" height="954" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
</ol><p>After you connect to Google, the <a href="#h_01K8XK5T5197JY8GPMDEYAASKQ">Google Ads connector tools</a> become available in <a href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/36343492268813" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Opal Chat</a>, <a href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/39407442255245" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">agents</a>, and <a href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/39417564742797" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">workflows</a>.</p><h2 id="h_01K8XK5T5197JY8GPMDEYAASKQ">Google Ads connector tools<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01K8XK5T5197JY8GPMDEYAASKQ"></a></h2><p>After an Opal administrator <a href="#h_01K8VBDBEWF17NE7XV6EC8CG70">installs the Opal Google Ads Tool in OCP</a> and you <a href="#h_01KKCNWPHE41X467Y5YG4C9WV7">authenticate with Google Ads</a>, call the following tools in Opal. Click a tool to expand it and learn when to use it, available parameters, and example prompts. If you do not provide a required parameter, Opal prompts you for it.</p><h3 id="h_01KTYKRN36ERCSTK7834WGJE89">Account access and verification<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KTYKRN36ERCSTK7834WGJE89"></a></h3><p>Use these tools to confirm which Google Ads account is connected and to discover all accounts available to you. This is especially useful for manager (MCC) accounts with multiple sub-accounts, and as a first step before running queries against a specific account.</p><details><summary><code>google_ads_get_account_info</code> – Get information about the connected Google Ads account.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e2f23577cf57bd7f7647ab3c53088d3d2">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eeaad90ef98e493d1d5fd60d1631939b6">Confirm which account is connected before running other queries.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebff39367fbea5f315546ab1c245a3d8f">Retrieve the account name, customer ID, currency code, and timezone of a specific Google Ads account.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3b360e4a4d78afdf298765132c708f40">Check the manager status and auto-tagging configuration of an account.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eaa1b822db2422269ef9c4ec5ac239dd0">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="ef6a070e6163e8589e171dff12839416a">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Google Ads Customer ID to query (digits only, no hyphens). For example, <code>1234567890</code>. Default: Uses the Customer ID from authentication settings. Only needed if querying a different account than the default.</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e0ee3479a67a46aeafb8a9fb87788302f">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e8f0a30e41643f3b7cc6337c27467a8a5"><em>Get the current Google Ads account info.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e1b5ae797a50a8da367f083eb21b5d7d3"><em>Can you tell me the timezone and currency for customer ID 1234567890?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e06d5d3f920803fd6fc3fded5b91ea4a6"><em>Check the manager status of my connected Google Ads account.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_list_accessible_customers</code> – List all Google Ads customer accounts accessible with the current credentials.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eb37cae605b4f87a1c1c8f87b16b5835b">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eb50a8fcf223cf6d89203a7cd3afd9ac8">Discover sub-accounts available under a MCC account.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e51a44e8702890dabb53cf2a0e8c3840a">Verify which customer accounts the authenticated user can access before querying specific IDs.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eeee6c726d44c263ee6dc1d49a0313959">Retrieve a list of accessible customer IDs to pass into other Google Ads tools like campaigns or keywords.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e5aefa07ac896251fc92fec7041c66e05">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="e41096df9d7480316961930e05c82950d">None</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea7c04327629721ccc765195e18aee2b0">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="efe5cb9369acd8473f34a95005c842df5"><em>List all the Google Ads accounts I have access to.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb0492baa6cb48a18e21d10e678f1274b"><em>What customer accounts can my credentials see?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e135f02f2e7b044253905a9b146b55ee5"><em>Show me all accessible customer IDs for my manager account.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><h3 id="h_01KKCQ11R46MYXQT9P5TCTBM3B">Campaign and structure management<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KKCQ11R46MYXQT9P5TCTBM3B"></a></h3><p>Use these tools to analyze the hierarchy of your Google Ads account, monitor high-level performance metrics, manage budgets, and drill into specific ad groups and ad creatives.</p><details><summary><code>google_ads_get_campaigns</code> – Get high-level campaign metrics.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e0548a53059a91302c7db88f75ba6c4d0">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e9e9007551f91e73d579482bf2c63b681">Monitor total spend, impressions, and conversions for specific campaigns over a set date range.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e64909828e94d9bb6a5a78d2b00a5c5d3">Compare performance between active and paused campaigns.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efacea892304e8b6bb644008169435484">Identify top-performing campaigns to inform budget reallocation.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e2f72bc5646559693a38ba0f31d31e762">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e6df1748399fbddfa09b4f88b2228e702">(Optional) <code>startDate</code> – Date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. For example, <code>2025-01-01</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1ea46fc13c1fa20f93c55583c23432f0">(Optional) <code>endDate</code> – Date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. For example, <code>2025-01-31</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7d20236e5ef31d5537c79dc82c6ce2c9">(Optional) <code>campaignIds</code> – JSON array of campaign IDs to filter by. For example, <code>[12345678, 87654321]</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed73b45bbae6a1e67816cc909816824f4">(Optional) <code>metrics</code> – JSON array of metric names to include. For example, <code>['impressions', 'clicks', 'cost_micros', 'ctr', 'conversions']</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e550c0f7b5442991a4de13647a2ba0dd1">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Customer ID (digits only).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0a1112bf44c74eeef32648c86cf3d3f3">(Optional) <code>campaignStatus</code> – JSON array of campaign statuses to filter by. Provide as a JSON string. For example, single status: <code>['ENABLED']</code>, multiple statuses: <code>['ENABLED', 'PAUSED']</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eacb97977423cf2f73cfbf4a4717f32ae">(Optional) <code>campaignName</code> – Filter campaigns by name (case-insensitive contains match). </li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ecc894070a896e9aa0de8c6f62e47bafa">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e9039460298d6a793ac372eca31561d70"><em>Show me the total cost and conversions for all enabled campaigns last month.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e59f5ba660dad95f8db39576d4124ac51"><em>How did my "Search - Brand" campaign perform over the last 14 days?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ef926f6da58366b18e678ca7b3078c84a"><em>I need a list of all paused campaigns and their historical click-through rates.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_get_adgroups</code> – Get ad group performance information.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e705bf3761797499c89edf24dd846611c">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="efb16db8465be118fddb7b4fbeadd1457">Break down campaign results to see which themes or ad groups drive the most ROI.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e65bbb4eac7f904d7cb1be233b42e1067">Analyze conversion rates at the ad group level to identify optimization opportunities.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebf7c8ef750b75b89d8140b6684398656">Filter by ad group status to review performance of specific experimental groups.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e180fdb89127da5af65e37d94ad49628f">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ebf2783d745182fccac4bda96ead59e03">(Optional) <code>startDate</code> – Date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. For example, <code>2025-01-01</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e057f1922d565ab6ae21ecf4f89324f65">(Optional) <code>endDate</code> – Date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. For example, <code>2025-01-31</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec58367e0ed1e3cec77e49caac39d7dd6">(Optional) <code>campaignIds</code> – JSON array of campaign IDs to filter by. For example, <code>[12345678, 87654321]</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0f276ff7d3d04a4c0b813decf1a3de8b">(Optional) <code>metrics</code> – JSON array of metric names to include. For example, <code>['impressions', 'clicks', 'cost_micros', 'ctr', 'conversions']</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e895d7f26b6a334599930fd7913cc436a">(Optional) <code>adGroupIds</code> – JSON array of ad group IDs to filter by. For example, <code>[98765432, 87654321]</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e30728fd569f7f3d31f9aaa40273bfae4">(Optional) <code>adGroupStatus</code> – JSON array of ad group statuses to filter by.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e146031a83a12d6fef041a5787069e049">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Customer ID (digits only).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e192579bd67cddaae5f8dc017c4230d1f">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ee93860912d1473eb6d55456601be0f67"><em>What are the top five ad groups by conversion rate in my "Winter Sale" campaign?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e204c28aea5e750f11f824c197251bc2d"><em>Show me the impressions and CPC for ad groups in campaign ID 12345.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e49f58fada1b4c32b81d845499debbfd7"><em>List all enabled ad groups that had more than 10 conversions last week.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_get_ads</code> – Get individual ad performance.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e939061864ed72dddf48e922581713a62">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eff2cb96caa2788e92b6e9c34189789fe">Evaluate the performance of specific Responsive Search Ads or Expanded Text Ads.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed33d7a025af47edb71e7037e5dee2b2a">Identify which ad creatives have the highest CTR.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee7abe9ae2db8be6557fe16ee1ad498d9">Audit the performance of active ads within a specific campaign to refine copy or assets.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ef3b4ac385ac3746747cb7af2f92e8a15">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e23a7fa315307354a0450fae7bbb96fd6">(Optional) <code>startDate</code> – Date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. For example, <code>2025-01-01</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef6417addac8b631921458497bde9e193">(Optional) <code>endDate</code> – Date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. For example, <code>2025-01-31</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e4bcc0d7be540ad8ac74eafdf8ff2a33d">(Optional) <code>campaignIds</code> – JSON array of campaign IDs to filter by. For example, <code>[12345678, 87654321]</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e01894ae014d596debce7678e71dde901">(Optional) <code>metrics</code> – JSON array of metric names to include. For example, <code>['impressions', 'clicks', 'cost_micros', 'ctr', 'conversions']</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e71a51b8672c902a2d0a1175698fad45d">(Optional) <code>adIds</code> – JSON array of ad IDs to filter by. For example, <code>[11111111, 22222222]</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e632acd8d77619168ca0d2905451214bf">(Optional) <code>adGroupIds</code> – JSON array of ad group IDs to filter by. For example, <code>[98765432, 87654321]</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e64209b95a19b1ea5cd4c36129d35090f">(Optional) <code>adStatus</code> – JSON array of ad statuses to filter by. For example,<code> ['ENABLED', 'PAUSED']</code>. Valid statuses include <code>ENABLED</code>, <code>PAUSED</code>, and <code>REMOVED</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1ade3e156c51098e71c35297b7f83964">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Customer ID (digits only).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e034d0e685bea3feb5c8881c0eb415d61">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e78f2403b8d020b95fccd06bf197be363"><em>Compare the performance of all enabled ads in my "Brand" ad group.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e9dac2e7589b85974e681dd8cfcb6b5b5"><em>Which individual ads had the lowest cost per click (CPC) last month?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e41a5e9d07c7124b280dca85a112d4810"><em>Show me the conversion data for all ads in campaign 987654.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_get_budgets</code> – Get budget settings and spend.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e58cc185cdc38a877bf63e83d302b340b">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ee736c2117af2d13d7fc52233e354680a">Track how much of your daily budget your campaigns use.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5138ea5ec756467c9324a157506ae2c3">Monitor shared budget performance to ensure even delivery.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e51c3c8a4a7b5221029711f5fa3e025f3">Identify campaigns that are "Limited by Budget" by comparing cost to daily limits.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ef1194173fb05b403f88e1963e9e89ac5">

<li data-list-item-id="ebc1a32a697ee3034f8dfb3c70c8bae6c">Identify keywords with high cost but no conversions to pause or exclude.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee3ffc59ab4dde4e0e7914df2666ea269">Check Quality Score (Google's 1–10 rating of keyword relevance and ad experience) and expected click-through rate for keywords.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e9f6f2289d213c041bd7e6201997f18fd">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e5aab810ae37b2eef3a3979ea5b7ade44">(Optional) <code>startDate</code> – Date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. For example, <code>2025-01-01</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e96845676b012f27e2b7d12b75aabe197">(Optional) <code>endDate</code> – Date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. For example, <code>2025-01-31</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e13230224755e17408ef79d0216067925">(Optional) <code>metrics</code> – JSON array of metrics. For example, <code>['impressions', 'clicks', 'cost_micros', 'ctr', 'conversions', 'quality_score']</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9555c193d3710122911dad5a0b3c84fe">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Customer ID (digits only).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1114926a008fa6d55106204b2649b183">(Optional) <code>campaignIds</code> – JSON array of campaign IDs to filter by. For example, <code>[12345678, 87654321]</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef390a18674722560075b77feae3c99ba">(Optional) <code>keywordTexts</code> – JSON array of keyword texts to filter by. For example, <code>['running shoes', 'sneakers', 'athletic footwear']</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e96525930631d25257bcf29b151e60f1a">(Optional) <code>adGroupIds</code> – JSON array of ad group IDs to filter by. For example, <code>[98765432, 87654321]</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e4989542862550bf23cdc0b3094865e66">(Optional) <code>matchTypes</code> – JSON array of keyword match types to filter by. For example, <code>['EXACT', 'PHRASE']</code>. Valid match types include the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e4bc71555d3acaf7319731b8108a4dba3">
<code>EXACT</code> – Exact match keywords.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1aad0b23dae97c26e0794636f305479d">
<code>PHRASE</code> – Phrase match keywords.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef9429cbf35558c613675b4957f2e34ce">
<code>BROAD</code> – Broad match keywords.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>

</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_get_search_terms</code> – Get end-user search terms.</summary><ul>

<li data-list-item-id="e142b69c731e6e82365bb2b13ab356977">(Optional) <code>adGroupIds</code> – JSON array of ad group IDs. For example, <code>[12345678]</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ebc10e1a7c319dccf25dddbcfbb8e76ae">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e251d8d96b3cd993864f09b2dc248c7df"><em>Which gender segment has the highest CTR in my "Apparel" campaign?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ec01182d52623378b004645bfe17c1832"><em>Show me the conversion value breakdown by gender for campaign ID 445566.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e9601d836b2db1490b49d077b8a2bcaf4"><em>Compare impressions by gender for all search campaigns over the last 60 days.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_get_audiences</code> – Get audience configuration.</summary><ul>

<li data-list-item-id="ed9c483a5b4922e103f2f0ad5159b6b55">Audit audience definitions to ensure they align with your current marketing strategy.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed2c49876768be5ca7d8ee0b778e46576">Identify available audiences for re-marketing or lookalike targeting.</li>

</li>

<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e60a70fc6568b71c41ec4f67e2f59f451">(Optional) <code>audienceIds</code> – JSON array of audience IDs. For example, <code>[12345678, 87654321]</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e06b39f0bf9af58fc7916c84671c7be33">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Customer ID (digits only).</li>

</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eccadc55855b76c5e35fe501e1dd9327f">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eba67928df3a71806a06fc12d53032d32"><em>List all custom audiences configured in my account.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e0acd8a065f08b999449487d9646c8819"><em>What are the definitions for my current remarketing lists?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e623ab394180b2cfd533db422f6547513"><em>Show me the IDs for all "In-Market" audiences I am currently tracking.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><h3 id="h_01KKCQ11R5TS93SSZTC2X56463">Geographic and result tracking<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KKCQ11R5TS93SSZTC2X56463"></a></h3><p>These tools provide location-specific data and detailed conversion tracking insights. Use them to understand where your results come from and what actions users take.</p><details><summary><code>google_ads_get_geographic_performance</code> – Get location-based performance information.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e6adbc233ce2e66b82f5a929adfa2391b">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ee5dba5f3690a923f48c5a8eb3a3a506d">Identify high-performing countries, regions, or cities for expanded targeting.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec737fabe30e93464488bb55a5bb7d534">Determine which geographic areas should be excluded based on high spend and low conversions.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e324f1524f9df402270cfe8622c3b6091">Inform location-based bid adjustments for specialized local service campaigns.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e6bd45104d3cf4ee767749bb0a67af636">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e6d531dee209b817612331fe62720e68e">(Optional) <code>adGroupIds</code> – JSON array of ad group IDs to filter by. Examples include the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ee6a0edc1cef23ead6b166516f0f9b625">
<strong>Single ad group </strong>– <code>[12345678]</code>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7c766a42e2ea7a7ab0c246ec05bfe871">
<strong>Multiple ad groups</strong> – <code>[12345678, 87654321]</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef563ea55f8bc4a6fa9ae80d2b70fa9f0">(Optional) <code>locationIds</code> – JSON array of location criteria IDs to filter by. Examples include the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e00efadd17e501ea3925853f4ad5e92a0">
<strong>Single location</strong> – <code>[2840]</code> (United States).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efa8690c73dc2fd59bd41feea48a69549">
<strong>Multiple locations</strong> – <code>[2840, 2826, 2124]</code> (United States, United Kingdom, and Canada).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e515d5d9fc65f8107a726a147c26a415f">(Optional) <code>startDate</code> – Date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. For example, <code>2025-01-01</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edc17e177ef441ce6fe9921b8a503a56d">(Optional) <code>endDate</code> – Date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. For example, <code>2025-01-31</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb91cbdffe24b220f7c49c4b9ce7618a0">(Optional) <code>campaignIds</code> – JSON array of campaign IDs to filter by. Provide as a JSON string. Examples include the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e56e106a73995c2a0b83fbca089f246b1">
<strong>Single campaign </strong>– <code>[12345678]</code> </li>
<li data-list-item-id="e170f4328d3fea4cd2650ff8a00a59a60">
<strong>Multiple campaigns</strong> – <code>[12345678, 87654321]</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef7e01e52281e6c60993102ab51a02d00">(Optional) <code>metrics</code> – JSON array of metric names to include in the response. For example, <code>['metrics.impressions', 'metrics.clicks', 'metrics.cost_micros', 'metrics.ctr', 'metrics.conversions']</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ecaf4c398d05882572a2a06fbda351cb1">(Optional) <code>customerIds</code> – Google Ads Customer ID to query (digits only, no hyphens). For example, <code>1234567890</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e1a9ef4301a89c9c214100b8b3a19bef7">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ecf56efe1debd243fdc460f63fc6e34ce"><em>What were the top five countries by conversion rate for my "Global Search" campaign?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e29a4fd2b7c6f810715c5e59f6895a9ce"><em>Show me the cost per acquisition (CPA) for users in California versus New York over the last month.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="efb52229e760e69a6d9b540d511029f6b"><em>List all cities in the UK where my ads generated more than 50 clicks last week.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_get_conversions</code> – Get conversion action configuration data from Google Ads.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e5e21c0d39835ed81d9f8325246cdd6b4">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e8f995d915bd7c06f25370c5de6257dc2">Retrieve conversion tracking configuration to see which conversion actions are set up.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e85784254e1156b0b7031a20bc8e9fbf9">Check the categories, statuses, and types of your configured conversions.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e237adcb923890c8fcaabc2cb75359858">Filter specific conversion actions by category (for example, purchases or leads) to audit tracking setups.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e9ac59d5caada59a35ea5ec0ab06782aa">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e67e49e85e42b4a8ef16887a6cab47297">(Optional) <code>categories</code> – JSON array of conversion categories. Example: "['PURCHASE', 'LEAD']". Valid categories: PURCHASE, LEAD, SIGNUP, PAGE_VIEW, ADD_TO_CART, etc.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7046ae0785e39046ed5749d71d7e4aff">(Optional) <code>conversionActionIds</code> – JSON array of conversion action IDs. Example: "[12345678, 87654321]"</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5b1c277a4b2b9ca46f2bd67180d0fc1c">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Customer ID (digits only). Uses default if not provided</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="efef1d9699d39ae511ee634730a53b001">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e413a48e1bb823134aff9e359dc2020a2"><em>Get all conversion actions configured in my Google Ads account.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e761a0ad4eaca7672141c7c2ff7ed4cfa"><em>Show me the configuration for conversion action IDs 12345678 and 87654321.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e80171432a71c8c04b61007d2a4b19137"><em>List all the conversion actions that are categorized under 'PURCHASE' or 'LEAD'.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><h3 id="h_01KTYKTNFNK6W2757RT8AMN00N">Campaign and keyword management<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KTYKTNFNK6W2757RT8AMN00N"></a></h3><p>Use these tools to make changes to your account, such as pausing campaigns, adjusting budgets and bids, and adding keywords. Unlike the reporting tools, these tools modify your live campaigns and can affect spend, so review the changes before you apply them.</p><details><summary><code>google_ads_add_keywords</code> – Add keywords to a Google Ads ad group.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eaff5cf697c8bd450e8a5d03837c9a94c">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eaa801e0e2fce1370bcd5b049aee5db95">Create one or more keyword criteria in a specified ad group.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e14265173822744ad1fe6c7d4136d5332">Add multiple keywords with different match types (<code>EXACT</code>, <code>PHRASE</code>, or <code>BROAD</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed61301752b9f765be51c5248ca745487">Add keywords with a default cost-per-click (CPC) bid to an ad group.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e15a8f3ba7e9f29f915171fcff5407729">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e83f42d1eb1b71c86c1ea3380f64ac802">
<code>adGroupId</code> – The ad group ID to add keywords to. For example, <code>12345678</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e28305a222a9040fbb2ed71ed15b5b18f">
<code>keywords</code> – JSON array of keyword objects. Each object must have <code>text</code> and <code>matchType</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2f7102d2ab99d9d95b067a5ea9e7d231">(Optional) <code>cpcBidMicros</code> – Default CPC bid in micros for all keywords being added. 1,000,000 micros = $1.00.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e756b1c6174601c77b978d758d858f01d">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Google Ads Customer ID (digits only, no hyphens). Default: Uses the Customer ID from authentication settings.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e041b3c2cbdf0f1704ffe03b9dc273db5">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e41ab6997378f8618353d28f76df739d2"><em>Add the exact match keyword "running shoes" to ad group 12345678.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e58a81a4917ac2dfe713e01810baa75e2"><em>Can you add "best running shoes" as a phrase match and "athletic footwear" as broad match to ad group 12345678?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e157ab4d9a0340a6a5a751916e5a82e22"><em>Add the keyword "running shoes" with an exact match and a default CPC bid of $1.50 to ad group 12345678.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_update_keyword_bid</code> – Update the CPC bid for a keyword in a Google Ads ad group.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e68edb316d064beede2ce002ecb52b65b">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ef4e76fa8eb8b3919563025d3ad7855b0">Update the CPC bid amount for a specific keyword criterion.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3fffcacdb1c15a381b2b2c56dab849b1">Adjust bids in micros (1,000,000 micros = $1.00).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6e5a4eb5ba5254d7eb75cf6ffc4b705c">Change the bid for an individual keyword without affecting the entire ad group.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e9a7ac046bbc776c672d9f22557bfc700">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e191005232edb3cc7db66269abc447536">
<code>adGroupId</code> – The ad group ID that contains the keyword. For example, <code>12345678</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e01f8581fe5274c96c0c5fbcfa2e0c9c1">
<code>cpcBidMicros</code> – New CPC bid amount in micros. 1,000,000 micros = $1.00.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e854b425cac97b6070be70181a1ab954d">
<code>criterionId</code> – The keyword criterion ID to update the bid for. For example, <code>99887766</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e35fead1224af77ad2b570c0a24cfc10f">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Google Ads Customer ID (digits only, no hyphens). Default: Uses the Customer ID from authentication settings.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eed36b8367f90af7bbb6ffdbc3038297e">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e5c14d43e9e96f36bbd04454289b5e028"><em>Set the CPC bid to $1.50 for keyword criterion 99887766 in ad group 12345678.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e80c7fa89335070af6f18c8a00592c476"><em>Update the keyword bid to $0.50 for criterion 99887766 in ad group 12345678.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e762f4e21aee7cc8ce1c99ce67a899af1"><em>Change the CPC bid to $10.00 for keyword 99887766 in my ad group 12345678.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_update_keyword_status</code> – Pause or enable keywords in a Google Ads ad group.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea2b6e62544f6a42b8deaaf1d59d63875">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e2e359324bb2a63f58c4bc5dd09df366e">Update the status of one or more keyword criteria to <code>ENABLED</code> or <code>PAUSED</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ecafc6d76cb6fa59c0a8a9178fcf2220a">Pause a single underperforming keyword in an ad group.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1d26ddb58908bf3b3da2b2d8475192ef">Enable multiple keywords at once.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e9923c0ea43c2dbeb1c6278fa0e818376">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e13ce26f6c0214411ebde60576f17e19c">
<code>adGroupId</code> – The ad group ID that contains the keywords. For example, <code>12345678</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e12404a61753bf408f1166bec354f47a3">
<code>criterionIds</code> – JSON array of keyword criterion IDs to update. Provide as a JSON string.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef6edee121a04ff381cd823115e204da4">
<code>status</code> – New status for the keywords. Valid values: <code>ENABLED</code> or <code>PAUSED</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e059a532849caf1ccaf6987f340a7ab11">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Google Ads Customer ID (digits only, no hyphens). Default: Uses the Customer ID from authentication settings.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e366a3943b45d7a73502f408fb1bc081a">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e8df77afea89e75c1d9c40b57ca731bf9"><em>Pause keyword criterion 99887766 in ad group 12345678.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e2cac2bf8a53e62194a913adf8e1ce841"><em>Enable keyword criteria 99887766 and 55443322 in ad group 12345678.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e0f31a38286b0517abc285f643b6d73bb"><em>Please update the status to PAUSED for keyword 99887766 in ad group 12345678.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_update_ad_status</code> – Pause or enable Google Ads ads within an ad group.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea04b73c835728a34e4b4805eefca07e4">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e6789bff3438845e2a4a742f88601fdb6">Update the status of one or more ads to <code>ENABLED</code> or <code>PAUSED</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efc573209bf925715fa0db41dccf97708">Pause a single underperforming ad in an ad group.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea40c4bac17b7dcaaa6a511bbd566b665">Enable multiple ads at once within the same ad group.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e03a5a1d0e78063d4ddbcd091b46b5c67">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e438aa582954e6eed63ed24b13d438bc9">
<code>adGroupId</code> – The ad group ID that contains the ads. Required to construct the ad resource name. For example, <code>12345678</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e214b04f20b7a7c7886f43c1bb884529d">
<code>adIds</code> – JSON array of ad IDs to update. Provide as a JSON string.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e286053bb3587341a7a133d1236a5ed38">
<code>status</code> – New status for the ad(s). Valid values: <code>ENABLED</code> or <code>PAUSED</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e67aee45f50af610376bb925375440fa7">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Google Ads Customer ID (digits only, no hyphens). Default: Uses the Customer ID from authentication settings.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea25b0f1f1a2047c2fdb1a038eb8e4e93">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e04a3c388adfcdecbab96c6f7e0563846"><em>Pause ad 99887766 in ad group 12345678.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e124a35846a789b0f6d1dc331c5c088d8"><em>Enable ads 99887766 and 55443322 in ad group 12345678.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e1ca4b9838c80023544ef1a670f170c96"><em>Update the status to PAUSED for ad 99887766 in ad group 12345678.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>google_ads_update_adgroup_status</code> – Pause or enable Google Ads ad groups.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e94495b04854193d06e4a55e4a2b97e28">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ef1e8a790b812e841ca8a217ca25a086d">Update the status of one or more ad groups to <code>ENABLED</code> or <code>PAUSED.</code>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e405a8f1964b851912998a1a1baec0400">Pause a single ad group.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e4fc5b36ef2c3c980e9b6806f03de4b75">Enable multiple ad groups at once.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e48e4490f8639438b4178d730b3b182a8">

<li data-list-item-id="e1a8745355c7f40621dca45d83285a312">
<code>adGroupIds</code> – JSON array of ad group IDs to update. Provide as a JSON string.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e866665e6ada8d8c4191609bedd1bc3de">
<code>status</code> – New status for the ad groups. Valid values: <code>ENABLED</code> or <code>PAUSED</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5b2a98cb43ec95cad2fb32a6b0869c43">(Optional) <code>customerId</code> – Google Ads Customer ID (digits only, no hyphens). Default: Uses the Customer ID from authentication settings.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e8bdb424fd83b4a49eb1946fec299a3a6">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e04a4b7791691f9e7cf0917c688526c59"><em>Pause ad group 12345678.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb4de768f61f02699102880ff7f709d8b"><em>Enable ad groups 12345678 and 87654321.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e59361667de09d70b7ea4ad126cfc69fe"><em>Change the status to PAUSED for ad group 12345678.</em></li>

Google Ads connector tools – Support Help Center                   

[Skip to main content](#page-container)

The Google Ads connector tools in Optimizely Opal give you direct access to your advertising performance data. Use them to retrieve detailed metrics across campaigns, ad groups, and individual keywords. This integration lets you analyze audience demographics, geographic trends, and search queries to understand how your audience interacts with your ads. By centralizing these insights, you can optimize your budgets and refine targeting for Performance Max and Shopping campaigns. This supports data-backed experimentation and drives higher return on investment (ROI).

First, an [Opal administrator](/hc/en-us/articles/36359944449805) must [connect Opal with Google Ads](#h_01K8VBDBEWF17NE7XV6EC8CG70). After an administrator installs the connector in Optimizely Connect Platform (OCP), you can [log in to Google Ads](#h_01KKCNWPHE41X467Y5YG4C9WV7) from Opal to access your data. Administrators only need to install the Google Ads connection in OCP once.

## Use cases[](#h_01KKCTFGB8MSSJTHHTBYD0JBJX)

The following use cases show how you can use Google Ads connector tools in Opal to connect ad performance data with content and creative workflows.

### Marketing strategy and performance optimization[](#h_01KKCV15C39HR1NTJWDYZ8KTS4)

**Goal** – Data-driven budget allocation and campaign scaling.

*   **Key performance indicator (KPI) monitoring and budget shifting** – Use the `googleads_get_campaigns` and `googleads_get_budgets` tools to identify campaigns with high conversion rates but low impression share (the percentage of eligible impressions your ads receive). Opal can draft a recommendation to reallocate funds from budget-constrained campaigns.
*   **High-intent keyword discovery** – Run the `googleads_get_keywords` and `googleads_get_search_terms` tools to surface high-value search queries that drive conversions but are not yet added as exact-match keywords.
*   **Channel synergy analysis** – Compare performance across Search, Shopping (`googleads_get_shopping_performance`), and Performance Max (PMax) (`googleads_get_asset_groups`) to determine which network is most efficient for specific product categories.

### A/B experimentation[](#h_01KQHZMVCPSAZEP4MQMPKCHQPD)

**Goal** – Validate creative and copy hypotheses.

*   **Ad copy comparison** – Use the `googleads_get_ads` tool to compare the click-through rate (CTR) and conversion rate of different Responsive Search Ads (RSAs). Opal can analyze which headlines or descriptions drive performance and suggest variations for follow-up testing.
*   **Landing page validation** – Correlate specific ad groups (`googleads_get_adgroups`) with conversion data to see which landing pages (mapped to those ad groups) are underperforming. Use this to trigger an Optimizely Web Experimentation or Optimizely Feature Experimentation test on those pages.
*   **Demographic sensitivity testing** – Use the `googleads_get_age_performance` and `googleads_get_gender_performance` tools to see if a specific creative resonates better with certain age groups. If a "Gen Z" creative is underperforming with its target, Opal can draft a brief for a more aligned creative direction.

### Content pipeline and creative plans[](#h_01KQHZMVCQMDTHWB3WDRCBDE97)

**Goal** – Use search data to fuel Optimizely Content Marketing Platform (CMP).

*   **Search-driven content briefs** – Analyze top-performing search terms using the `googleads_get_search_terms` tool. If a specific question or pain point appears frequently, Opal can generate a brief for a blog post in CMP to address that topic through organic search content.
*   **PMax asset optimization** – Use the `googleads_get_asset_groups` tool to identify which asset groups in a Performance Max campaign have "Low" performance ratings. Opal can then help generate image prompts or headlines to replace the weak assets.
*   **Seasonal creative refresh** – Pull geographic performance data using the `googleads_get_geographic_performance` tool. If a region is showing an uptick in interest for a specific product, use Opal to create localized ad copy or social assets tailored to that region's trends.

### Audience insights and target strategy[](#h_01KQHZMVCQ0B6XA3A2BZDMHK42)

**Goal** – Refine your audience and your geography.

*   **Geographic expansion** – Identify cities or regions with high conversion rates but low volume using the `googleads_get_geographic_performance` tool. Use this insight to create localized landing page content or localized ad extensions.
*   **Audience mapping** – Use the `googleads_get_audiences` tool to see which user lists are assigned. Opal can suggest **Similar Segments** or **In-Market** audiences based on the characteristics of the customers who convert at the highest rate.

## Connect Opal with Google Ads[](#h_01K8VBDBEWF17NE7XV6EC8CG70)

### Install the Opal Google Ads Tool in OCP[](#h_01KKC744XBD3CEE52R72N99D5K)

In the OCP **App Directory**, complete the following:

1.  Click the **Opal Google Ads Tool**.
    
    ![Screenshot of the OCP App Directory with the Opal Google Ads Tool tile highlighted.](/hc/article_attachments/45868019597325)
    
2.  Click **Install App**.
    
    ![Screenshot of the Opal Google Ads Tool Overview with the Install App button highlighted.](/hc/article_attachments/45868019598093)
    

### Configure Google Ads API authentication[](#h_01KKC7B334QC0GGNHJW16XQ0J2)

Configure the Google Ads API authentication so Opal can call Google Ads on behalf of your account.

1.  Select the **Settings** tab.
2.  Expand the **Google Ads API Authentication** section.
3.  Enter your **Customer ID**. See [Find your Google Ads customer ID](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1704344?hl=en) in the Google documentation for instructions.
4.  (Optional) Enter your **Login Customer ID**. If you manage multiple Google Ads accounts under a Manager account (a single login that controls several customer accounts), this is the Manager account ID. To find it, see the Additional tips to find your customer ID section in the [Find your Google Ads customer ID](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1704344?hl=en) in the Google documentation.
5.  Click **Save**.
    
    ![Screenshot of the Google Ads configuration in OCP with the Google ads API Authentication section expanded with the Save button highlighted.](/hc/article_attachments/45868019601293)
    

### Configure tool permissions[](#h_01KEJDK4GBA19AQV4ENMWND9AK)

1.  Select the **Settings** tab.
2.  Expand the **Tool Permissions** section.
3.  Toggle **Enable Data Reading** on to enable read-only tools.
4.  Toggle **Enable Data Modifications** on to enable write tools.
5.  Click **Save**.
    
    ![Google Ads OCP configuration with the Tools Permissions section expanded.](/hc/article_attachments/45868194896269)

### Account access and verification[](#h_01KTYKRN36ERCSTK7834WGJE89)

Use these tools to confirm which Google Ads account is connected and to discover all accounts available to you. This is especially useful for manager (MCC) accounts with multiple sub-accounts, and as a first step before running queries against a specific account.

`google_ads_get_account_info` – Get information about the connected Google Ads account.

*   **When to use**
    *   Confirm which account is connected before running other queries.
    *   Retrieve the account name, customer ID, currency code, and timezone of a specific Google Ads account.
    *   Check the manager status and auto-tagging configuration of an account.
*   **Parameters**
    *   (Optional) `customerId` – Google Ads Customer ID to query (digits only, no hyphens). For example, `1234567890`. Default: Uses the Customer ID from authentication settings. Only needed if querying a different account than the default.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Get the current Google Ads account info._
    *   _Can you tell me the timezone and currency for customer ID 1234567890?_
    *   _Check the manager status of my connected Google Ads account._

*   **When to use**
    *   Discover sub-accounts available under a MCC account.
    *   Verify which customer accounts the authenticated user can access before querying specific IDs.
    *   Retrieve a list of accessible customer IDs to pass into other Google Ads tools like campaigns or keywords.
*   **Parameters**
    *   None
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all the Google Ads accounts I have access to._
    *   _What customer accounts can my credentials see?_
    *   _Show me all accessible customer IDs for my manager account._
